messages:
Carla: heads up — seeing a weird preempt/evict wave in us-west2 this morning, looks like ~120 small gpu pods got killed in a 3m window :grimacing:
Anil: ack, saw alerts. any pattern on labels/affinity?
Carla: mostly ai-train-* jobs, lots of nodeSelector: gpu-type:nv5, and a mix of podAntiAffinity for same-team sets
Jin: also noticed a backlog in the warm pool resync queue — warm node churn spiked right before the evicts
Carla: logs from scheduler look like a flurry of lease timeouts + immediate preempt attempts:
```
I0311 07:12:14 scheduler.go:201] lease handshake failed: timeout
I0311 07:12:15 scheduler.go:344] attempt preempt: pod ai-train-42 -> victim candidate node-17
I0311 07:12:15 scheduler.go:346] preempt: sent SIGTERM to pod ai-train-13
I0311 07:12:16 scheduler.go:349] preempt backoff not respected, queuing immediate retry
```
Anil: ugh — backoff not honored would explain tight loop. any NIC/conntrack noise? that could cause lease acks to not arrive
Jin: yes, conntrack entries for ip range 10.4.* doubled, and conntrack drops on nodes with high pod churn
Maya: opsbot shows a concurrent rack-provision event in us-west2-b 07:11:50 — ephemeral capacity rebalancer ran and triggered taint drains to coalesce racks
Carla: that drifted many pods and left a bunch of tiny slots fragmented across racks, then scheduler tried to re-pack with strict podAntiAffinity -> triggered preempt cascade
Anil: TL;DR: fragmentation + taint-driven drains + broken preempt backoff + conntrack flakiness = eviction storm
Maya: can we short-term mute evicts for low-priority small pods? maybe patch preempt window to 30s? :thinking_face:
Jin: suggest immediate mitigations:
- setPreemptBackoff=true in scheduler config (was false in canary)
- bump conntrack max to 1.5x on warm nodes
- relax podAntiAffinity "requiredDuringScheduling" -> preferred for ai-train-* for next 2 hours
Carla: rolling a canary to flip setPreemptBackoff now. prepping PR with config patch.
Anil: if we do that, we should also prevent warm pool autoscaler from draining racks for 15m to avoid repeated fragmentation
Maya: ops, I'm holding off the warm-pool-destructor job for us-west2 for 20m — pausing now :pause_button:
OpsBot: warm-pool-destructor job paused by Maya for 20 minutes. Reason: emergency eviction storm mitigation.
Carla: after flipping backoff we need to replay scheduler logs to confirm no tight-loop preempts, watch eviction rate metric: cluster.evictions.rate
Jin: will run quick query: `sum(rate(kube_pod_container_status_terminated_reason{reason="Evicted"}[1m])) by (node)` and post results in 5m
Anil: long term we should add an anti-storm guard: if >X node drains in Y minutes in same AZ, throttle taint drains and convert required affinities to preferred for small-batch jobs automatically
Maya: also add conntrack health probe on the node exporter, alert when drops/s > 100 -> auto-scale conntrack or recycle node
Carla: PR link: https://github.com/redwood-inference/kube-configs/pull/876 (flip preempt backoff + preempt jitter). can someone review fast? :pray:
Anil: reviewing now, will lgtm if tests pass
Jin: posted eviction rate snapshot — peak 07:12:20 ~ 110 evicts/min across 6 nodes, now down to 4/min after pause
Carla: good. keeping watch. once stable we'll revert warm-pool pause and roll a more measured drain strategy
Maya: filing infra follow-up ticket (INFRA-2187) to track long-term anti-storm and affinity relaxation automation
Carla: thanks all — ping if anything flips back. :thumbsup:
